name: C. SHANNON BACON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that Intrepid's prolonged non-use and speculation demonstrated an intent to abandon most of its water rights, consistent with the constitutional mandate of beneficial use.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the affidavit provided sufficient factual detail from the CI's first-hand observations to establish probable cause for a search warrant for possession of methamphetamine, and that the Court of Appeals' misreading of Belknap was not fatal to its holding.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Dissented, argued that the affidavit failed to provide sufficient factual detail to establish probable cause for trafficking, merely stating a conclusion, and that the warrant was overbroad, authorizing seizure of items beyond what was supported by probable cause for possession.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Concurred, argued that judicial immunity is available to public bodies under the CRA, but the Court of Appeals erred in finding NMRC immune without sufficient factual inquiry into the nature of the proceedings and conduct.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that Stewart is entitled to legislative immunity for reassigning Candelaria's office and seat, as these are legitimate legislative activities, and her motives are irrelevant.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that a contempt fine payable to a third party is permitted under the judiciary's inherent contempt power and is constitutional because fines are not fees and were not collected by the judicial department.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the emergency orders for gun violence and drug abuse were largely valid exercises of the Governor's authority under PHERA and police power, except for the suspension of the JDAI program.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation of 'public health emergency' removed the 'emergency' aspect, granting the Governor unbridled discretion without requiring a true, sudden, or unforeseen crisis.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation of PHERA conferred unlimited emergency powers to the Governor, violating separation of powers by delegating excessive discretionary authority to the executive.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that public schools are public accommodations under the NMHRA, affirming the Court of Appeals and overruling prior inconsistent precedent.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that district courts have inherent authority and jurisdiction to sua sponte raise suppression issues for warrantless searches to protect fundamental rights, and such actions do not violate separation of powers or inherently demonstrate bias.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Dissented, argued that while district courts have inherent authority to protect fundamental rights, the district court abused its discretion by acting as an advocate, prejudging the outcome, and failing to maintain neutrality, thereby undermining the adversarial system.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General has the practical ability and implied statutory authority to obtain and produce documents from non-party executive agencies in state-interest civil litigation, and that this does not violate separation of powers.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the local ordinances are entirely preempted by state law, including the Reproductive and Gender-Affirming Health Care Freedom Act, Medical Practice Act, Medical Malpractice Act, Health Care Code, and Uniform Licensing Act, and granted the writ of mandamus.

name: JANE B. YOHALEM
description: Concurred, arguing that the Workers' Compensation Act's provisions for secondary mental impairments violate the Equal Protection Clause of the New Mexico Constitution by treating them differently than secondary physical impairments without substantial relation to an important government interest.

name: JULIE J. VARGAS
description: Concurred, argued that the authority to appropriate federal COVID-19 relief funds lies with the Legislature, not the Executive, based on the broad discretion given to states for these funds and the state constitution's appropriation clause.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that a district court judge has no authority at a preliminary examination to decide whether evidence was obtained from an unconstitutional search or seizure, as preliminary hearings are not the appropriate stage for such complex suppression issues.

name: BRETT R. LOVELESS, Judge Sitting by designation
MICHAEL E. VIGIL, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's conclusion contradicts basic principles of the New Mexico Constitution and fails to protect the accused's constitutional rights by preventing judges from considering the constitutionality of evidence at preliminary examinations.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion that partisan gerrymandering claims are justiciable under the New Mexico Constitution and established the standards for adjudication.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the amendment did not violate the single-measure rule or have a misleading ballot title, and the petition for writ of mandamus was denied.

name: JULIE J. VARGAS
description: Concurred, arguing that the defendant's seizure was unreasonable under the New Mexico Constitution due to a lack of reasonable suspicion.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that New Mexico's groundwater forfeiture statute allows for partial forfeiture, as mandated by the constitutional doctrine of beneficial use, which requires continuous use for water rights.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Concurred, argued that the public's right to recreate and fish in public water includes the right to touch privately owned beds below those waters.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Concurred, argued that the State failed to meet its evidentiary burden to justify pretrial detention and that the constitutional standard requiring proof that no release conditions would reasonably protect community safety cannot be lessened.

name: VIGIL, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that judicial conduct can bar retrial under the New Mexico Constitution's double jeopardy clause and that the judge's conduct in this case met the Breit test criteria, thus barring the defendant's retrial.

name: VIGIL, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the arrest was unconstitutional under Article II, Section 10 of the New Mexico Constitution, requiring suppression of evidence.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that the ETA is constitutional, does not violate due process, separation of powers, or other constitutional provisions, and that the Commission's finding regarding the securities firm memorandum was reasonable and supported by evidence.

name: BACON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that public health orders are a reasonable exercise of police power to prevent public injury and do not constitute a compensable taking under constitutional or statutory provisions.

name: VIGIL, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the MMA nonmedical, nonpunitive damages cap does not violate the constitutional right to trial by jury because it merely gives legal consequence to the jury's finding on damages and does not infringe the guarantee of Article II, Section 12.

name: JUDITH K. NAKAMURA, Justice, Retired, Sitting by designation
CONRAD F. PEREA, Judge, Sitting by designation
THOMSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that summary judgment was improper due to disputed material facts regarding substantial interference and that consequential damages for lost lease value may be compensable.

name: JUDITH K. NAKAMURA, Justice, Retired Sitting by designation
STEVEN BLANKINSHIP, Judge Sitting by designation
NAKAMURA, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the executive branch is authorized to impose business restrictions during a pandemic and that the temporary closure of indoor dining was not arbitrary or capricious.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that while the executive's actions were a proper exercise of emergency authority, broad and vague statutes granting such powers may pose long-term consequences to checks and balances, and judicial deference should wane as a crisis continues.
